### 8.3.4 Doctrinal Legal Construction and the Reconstruction of Individual Sovereignty

Confronting the destructive reality of algorithmic psychological manipulation, positive civil law doctrines in Indonesia and across global jurisdictions must undergo a progressive and radical reconstruction. Historically, our civil law framework—specifically Article 1320 of the Indonesian Civil Code (Burgerlijk Wetboek) regarding the validity of contracts, and Article 1321 concerning defects of will (*vitiated consent*) arising from mistake (*dwaling*), duress (*bedreiging*), or fraud (*bedrog*)—along with the Anglo-Saxon doctrine of *undue influence* (*misbruik van omstandigheden*), has been predicated on the classical liberal assumption that legal subjects are rational beings possessing pure autonomous free will, unencumbered by systematic external cognitive intervention (Hildebrandt, 2015).

When a large language model systematically erodes an individual’s mental autonomy through massively personalized emotional manipulation, that free will is vitiated at the cognitive source (Farahany, 2023). Consequently, the law must expand the interpretation of "defects of will" to encompass manipulations of artificial neural architectures that systematically impair the cognitive and affective capacities of legal subjects. This expansion ensures that contracts or legal acts born from such manipulation are voidable by operation of law (Article 1328 of the Indonesian Civil Code).

At the international regulatory level, frameworks such as the *European Union Artificial Intelligence Act* (EU AI Act) 2024 have taken a revolutionary step through Articles 5 and 50, which explicitly prohibit AI practices employing subliminal, manipulative, or deceptive techniques that materially alter human behavior in ways that cause, or are highly likely to cause, significant physical or psychological harm (EU AI Act, Regulation 2024/1689).

In Indonesia, this mandate must be translated into binding revisions or implementing regulations under the umbrella of the Indonesian Personal Data Protection Act (Law No. 27/2022) and the Electronic Information and Transactions Law (ITE Law). Protection of cognitive and affective profiles must be elevated to a new fundamental constitutional right—namely, the right to mental integrity and cognitive sovereignty (Farahany, 2023). The state is obligated to ensure that cognitive data is not freely traded as a commodity without explicit consent based on complete information (*informed consent*) (Indonesian Personal Data Protection Act, Law No. 27/2022, Article 20).

This doctrinal construction mandates *Psychological Safety Certification* as an absolute prerequisite for the commercial market authorization of any artificial intelligence system that interacts directly with the general public (Calo, 2014). This certification is not merely a bureaucratic administrative stamp, but the result of rigorous forensic linguistic and computational audits conducted by independent bodies accredited by the state (Floridi, 2013).

If a technology corporation launches a model proven to trigger psychological damage, pathological addiction, or destructive behavioral manipulation, a regime of *strict liability*—requiring no proof of fault—must be applied without exception. This liability must pierce the corporate veil directly to the executive directors, data scientists, and algorithm designers who consciously disregarded public safety standards in pursuit of short-term financial gain (Article 1338 of the Indonesian Civil Code; Article 1365 of the Indonesian Civil Code).

Ultimately, the reconstruction of individual sovereignty in the digital era demands that the state cease to remain passive within the ivory tower of obsolete classical legal dogmatism (Jonas, 1979). The state must emerge as a protective shield, ensuring that even the most sophisticated algorithms remain subordinate to the supreme law of civilization: the safety, dignity, and mental health of humanity (Buber, 1923).

True sovereignty in the 21st century is measured not only by how securely our physical data is stored within encrypted servers, but by how free our souls, minds, and emotions remain from the invisible grip of manipulation within the silent spaces of artificial discourse (Weizenbaum, 1976; Farahany, 2023).
